label: A von Bertalanffy grower stays strictly below its asymptotic length, and K alone sets the shape
statement_en: For a cohort whose length at age follows von Bertalanffy, length(t) = Linf*(1 - exp(-K*(t - t0))) with asymptotic length Linf > 0 and Brody coefficient K > 0 (a named hypothesis), length is strictly below Linf at every age, strictly increasing in age, and two cohorts sharing K reach the same fraction of their own asymptote at the same age measured from their own t0, however different their asymptotic lengths.

asymptotic_length.unit: cm (FL or TL as given per row)

scope.basis: 12 FishBase von Bertalanffy rows over 7 of the 75 Exocoetidae species, compiled in development/growth.json (built 2026-10-31); the default curve is the single row FishBase marks as validated. Field fits already embed the food and temperature of their locality (development/growth.json 'conditions' says nothing is adjusted for temperature or nutrition), so this is not a temperature-free law of growth. Nothing is established for the 68 species with no growth row, nor for embryos, for which no growth row exists. The theorem itself is taxon-free; the scope is the data the constants and the witness come from.
